title: Connection pool exhaustion: the datastore stops completing new connections

problem.summary: Something holds connections open against a datastore until the server will accept no more. The answer is the DATASTORE, not the thing holding the connections. The datastore stays alive and keeps serving its existing clients, so it does not go quiet and it does not saturate - what stops is the per-connection setup work it does for each NEW client. A container that appears and talks mostly on the network is the holder; naming it answers the wrong question.
symptoms: callers of a datastore fail or time out while the datastore itself looks healthy
the symptom is about connection availability, not query latency
the datastore keeps serving existing clients

discriminators.signal: per-connection setup syscalls inside the datastore - getpeername, gettid and access - as a rate, incident window against its own baseline
discriminators.this_problem: they collapse while the container keeps running: 169-177/s before against 0.0-0.9/s during, a ratio of 0.00-0.01, in 3 of 3 runs. The container that collapses IS the exhausted datastore and is the answer to WHERE
discriminators.not_this_problem: the datastore goes silent altogether - that is a stopped dependency, not an exhausted pool. An exhausted pool keeps serving the clients it already has
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED 28-09-2026 across 6 runs on two applications. Ranked the target first among containers doing per-connection work in 3 of 3 runs on the application where the datastore does such work at all.

discriminators.signal: a container present in the window and absent before it, talking on the network
discriminators.this_problem: the holder: about a third of its events are network and its futex share is zero, measured 36% and 0%. It corroborates, and it tells you WHAT is exhausting the pool
discriminators.not_this_problem: naming this container as the root cause. It is the agent of the fault, not the exhausted resource. The answer is the datastore whose setup work collapsed

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the exhausted pool can be seen from the datastore side
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: we measured the holder container only. Whether the datastore's own container shows a matching signature was not tested.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: do not claim it. Name the holder, not the victim.

reproduction.teardown: the recipe restores state; verify against /sys/fs/cgroup
harness_only: the fault is injected as a sidecar container, which is a property of our harness. In production the same mechanism occurs inside an existing service - so the SHAPE transfers, the newcomer shortcut does not

collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. Every discriminator in this blueprint is a share of these event groups within one container. Nothing else in the trace is required, and no other modality is used - this blueprint was built and validated on kernel traces alone.

processing.expect: a CTF directory with metadata and channel streams

processing.step: Find containers that are active during the window and absent before it
processing.expect: one container with substantial traffic during the window and none before. If none appears, this blueprint does not apply - say so and stop

processing.step: rank containers by how far their per-connection setup rate fell, counting only those that were doing such work before the window
processing.expect: containers that were establishing connections, ranked by the collapse in that work, the steepest named by pid_ns, with its before and after rates

processing.step: Measure what share of its own events that container spends on each kind of work
processing.expect: the share profile below, within the measured range

processing.step: Apply the rules and emit the verdict
processing.expect: name the DATASTORE by its pid_ns, its setup rate before and during, and separately name the holder container if one appeared
one page showing the shares, the cut, and what was ruled out

outputs.contains: culprit container pid_ns, its event shares, and the shares of every other container for comparison
per-container event shares for the window
each family's measured share on the deciding axis, with this run's value marked

verdict_when: a container was doing at least {SETUP_BASELINE_MIN_PER_S} per-connection setup syscalls per second before the window
that rate falls to {SETUP_COLLAPSE_MAX} or less of itself during the window, while the container keeps producing other events
the container did NOT go silent overall - an exhausted pool still serves its existing clients

rule_out.when: the container went silent altogether rather than only stopping new connections - a stopped dependency does no work at all
the datastore still completes new connections at its usual rate and is merely slow - that is latency, not exhaustion
you are about to name the container that APPEARED. That one is holding the connections; the answer is the datastore it is holding them against

decision.root_cause_is: the datastore whose per-connection setup work collapsed, named by its pid_ns. The container that appeared is the holder and is not the answer

provenance.authored_by: measured from StrataTrace v2 kernel traces
provenance.notes: Rewritten 28-09-2026. The generated version concluded on the container that was NEW to the window, which is the holder; ground truth names the datastore. Measured the datastore instead: its per-connection setup syscalls fall from 169-177/s to 0.0-0.9/s while it keeps running, ranking it first in 3 of 3 runs. On the second application the datastore does 0.7-1.1 such calls/s at baseline because its callers hold pooled connections, so the signature is absent there and the blueprint now says the check is not applicable rather than pointing elsewhere.

apply_when: callers of a datastore fail or time out while the datastore is not slow
the datastore is still running rather than stopped
the datastore was establishing new connections at a steady rate before the window
do_not_apply_when: the suspect container went silent - that is a stopped dependency

no container was doing per-connection setup work before the window. Where callers hold pooled connections that are already established, a datastore does almost no setup work and this blueprint can see nothing - measured 0.7-1.1 calls/s on such a system against 169-177 where it works. Report that the check was not applicable rather than naming another container
applicability.cheap_precheck: find containers doing at least {SETUP_BASELINE_MIN_PER_S} getpeername/gettid/access calls per second before the window, then see whether any fell to {SETUP_COLLAPSE_MAX} or less of that during it

capabilities_required.why: WHERE: the exhausted datastore is the target, and this is the only measured signal that names it rather than naming the holder.

stopping_conditions.conclude: a container that was doing per-connection setup work fell to {SETUP_COLLAPSE_MAX} or less of its own rate while still producing other events
stopping_conditions.stop_and_switch: the container went silent altogether, which is a stopped dependency; or its setup rate held, which means the pool is not exhausted
stopping_conditions.stop_insufficient: no container reached {SETUP_BASELINE_MIN_PER_S} setup calls per second in the baseline. Say the check was not applicable on this system - do not substitute another signal

applicable_symptoms: callers of one datastore start failing or timing out
the datastore itself is not busy
the failure is about availability of connections, not latency

historical_effectiveness.note: shares measured on 5 runs of this family

evidence_sufficiency.if_below_floor: report the per-container setup rates before and during, and say whether any container was doing enough of that work to judge
evidence_sufficiency.report_when_stuck: the ranked setup-rate table with the pid_ns of each container
